newsitem.title: UK: LVMH buys Grand Met shares, bid ruled out.
newsitem.headline: LVMH buys Grand Met shares, bid ruled out.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH said on Tuesday it had bought shares in Grand Metropolitan Plc but has no intention of making an offer the for British drinks group.

In a surprise move LVMH, which is trying to block a planned merger between Grand Met and Guinness Plc, said it now owns 0.23 percent of GrandMet after buying 4.75 million GrandMet shares at an average price of 577 pence per share.
GrandMet and LVMH were not immediately available for comment.
The move comes hard on the heels of LVMH's request last week for an arbitration proceeding to settle the row with Guinness in which LVMH holds a 14.2 percent stake.

LVMH contends it has the right to buy Guinness's stake in their joint distribution ventures and in champagne and spirits group Moet Hennessy if Guinness goes ahead with the GrandMet merger which, if approved, would be the biggest in UK corporate history.

The complex merger is also being closely watched by the European Commission, which is still considering whether to start a full probe into the proposed 24 billion pounds ($39.3 billion) merger, the largest in British corporate history.
LVMH's main argument against the merger is that that under the terms of agreements signed with Guinness a "control event" would enable LVMH to operate its joint ventures with Guinness independently.
Guinness has said that LVMH's claim lack any legal basis and is confident that the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), which will oversee arbitration, would agree.
